item.title: Harassment and security threats forced the cancellation of a Pride-themed community event in Malaysia
item.description: "This program was not cancelled because it was unlawful, but because an environment was created in which reckless rhetoric, misinformation and fear-mongering made it unsafe for people to gather."

item.title: Sly Dunbar, one half of the groundbreaking ‘Riddim Twins’ of Jamaican music, dies at 73
item.description: “Sly was an architect of sound. Alongside Robbie Shakespeare, he established a foundation that defined the era of Reggae and Dancehall.”

item.title: How to turn Africa’s young demographic potential into a collective power
item.description: The African youth, an exploding population, needs support and programs to turn their potential into economic power.

item.title: Pakistan’s Aafia Siddiqui and the elusive truth in a landscape of politicized narratives
item.description: The Islamabad High Court repeatedly rebuked Pakistani officials for using the case of Aafia Siddiqui as a symbolic political tool rather than pursuing a sustained legal strategy.

item.title: Tensions high in DRC, the global cobalt capital, between artisanal miners and industrial mining companies
item.description: Kolwezi in the Lualaba Province of the southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where tensions are high between artisanal miners and industrial companies, holds 70 percent of the world’s cobalt reserves.

item.title: Viral app ‘Are You Dead Yet?’ unveils the anxiety and pain of single Chinese youths
item.description: “Are You Dead Yet?” appealed to the psychology of the insecure youths, who don’t want to disturb others but wish that someone would pay attention to them when in need.

item.title: Off the scales: A Kurdish tale of absent justice in Syria
item.description: From Afrin to Aleppo, one family’s homes become bargaining chips amid displacement, extortion, and the lingering threat of violence.

item.title: Why India’s Aravalli Mountain Range matters: Interview with Anuradha P Dhawan
item.description: India’s Supreme Court’s redefinition of the Aravalli hills has triggered nationwide protests, with environmentalists warning that mining and real estate expansion could endanger India’s oldest mountain system and vulnerable communities.

item.title: Movement as solidarity: Walking for a cause across the U.S. and Britain
item.description: A Buddhist pilgrimage in the U.S. and a solidarity walk in the U.K. use long-distance walking as a nonconfrontational form of public peace witness.

item.title: Wasting renewable energy comes at a high cost for the Dominican Republic
item.description: By operating thermal plants above their limits and maintaining a grid with insufficient storage capacity, the DR wastes part of its clean energy and generates multimillion-dollar losses.
